prompt: What is an inset?

choices.text: A margin the designer adds around every screen
choices.why: Insets come from the system and the hardware, not from a design choice.

choices.text: A hole in the window where the app cannot draw
choices.why: The app can draw there, and should draw its background there; it keeps content out.

choices.text: How far in from an edge something covers the window
choices.why: Right. The status bar, the cutout, the gesture area and the keyboard are each reported that way.

choices.text: The density bucket of the screen
choices.why: Density is lesson 7's subject; an inset is a distance in dp or points.

prompt: Match each region to the edge where it usually sits on a phone held in portrait.

pairs.right: bottom, while a field has focus

prompt: Which Android inset type keeps content clear of every system interface at once?

choices.text: safeDrawing
choices.why: Right. It sums up the kinds content must not be drawn under.

choices.text: statusBars
choices.why: That covers the status bar alone.

choices.text: ime
choices.why: That is the keyboard alone.

choices.text: waterfall
choices.why: That is the curved edges of one kind of display.

prompt: What should the planner draw behind the status bar and the gesture area?

choices.text: Nothing; those regions belong to the system
choices.why: Leaving them empty makes the screen look cut off; the background goes there.

choices.text: The first rows of the session list
choices.why: Rows would be read under the clock or covered by the handle.

choices.text: The add-session button, so it is easy to reach
choices.why: A button under the gesture area competes with the system's own swipe.

choices.text: Its background colour, and nothing anyone reads or taps
choices.why: Right. Behind, but not under.

prompt: A list starts a status bar's height lower than intended, with an empty band above it, on Android only. What is the likeliest cause?

choices.text: The app ignored the insets
choices.why: Ignoring them puts the list under the status bar, the opposite symptom.

choices.text: The insets were applied twice
choices.why: Right. A component already padded, and the code padded again by hand.

choices.text: The screen's density is xxhdpi
choices.why: Density changes pixels per dp, not where the list starts.

choices.text: The phone is a foldable
choices.why: A fold does not add a band above the content.

prompt: From which Android API level is edge-to-edge enforced for an app that targets it?
What does SwiftUI do with a view's layout by default?

choices.text: Draws it edge to edge, and the app pads by hand
choices.why: That is a recent Android's default, not SwiftUI's.

choices.text: Keeps it out of certain safe areas
choices.why: Right. An app writes ignoresSafeArea to leave them on purpose.

choices.text: Centres it in a fixed 390-point column
choices.why: No fixed column exists; 390 was an example in this lesson's program.

choices.text: Hides the status bar while the app is open
choices.why: The status bar stays; the layout avoids it.

prompt: Match each tool to the platform it belongs to.
React Native's documentation marks its own SafeAreaView as deprecated. What does it point to?

choices.text: Padding every screen by 48 by hand
choices.why: A fixed number is wrong on most phones and in landscape.

choices.text: KeyboardAvoidingView
choices.why: That handles the keyboard, not the safe area.

choices.text: Locking the app to portrait
choices.why: Insets exist in portrait too.

choices.text: react-native-safe-area-context
choices.why: Right. Its SafeAreaView and useSafeAreaInsets report the insets on both platforms.

prompt: An Android app's screens looked right for years. After it targets SDK 35 and runs on Android 15, its title sits under the clock. What changed?

choices.text: It now draws edge to edge without the top inset
choices.why: Right. Before, the system kept it below the bars; now the app must.

choices.text: Android 15 made the status bar taller to fit more icons
choices.why: The bar's height is not the change.

choices.text: The density changed from xhdpi to xxhdpi
choices.why: Density does not move a title under the clock.

choices.text: The app must now be rewritten in SwiftUI
choices.why: SwiftUI is iOS; the fix is the inset.

prompt: In SwiftUI, a background that should extend under the status bar and the home indicator is given the modifier ___().
What does Android call the on-screen keyboard when it reports it as an inset?

choices.text: statusBars
choices.why: That is the status bar.

choices.text: displayCutout
choices.why: That is the notch or the camera hole.

choices.text: ime
choices.why: Right. The input method editor.

choices.text: navigationBars
choices.why: That is the gesture handle or the three buttons.

prompt: With the keyboard up, the planner's title field is visible but the add-session button is not. What is the general fix?

choices.text: Treat the keyboard as a bottom inset
choices.why: Right. The form's bottom edge becomes the top of the keys.

choices.text: Move the button to the top of the screen
choices.why: It would avoid the keyboard and land under the status bar, and far from the field.

choices.text: Close the keyboard as soon as the field gets focus
choices.why: Then nobody can type the title.

choices.text: Make the button 48 dp taller
choices.why: A taller button is still under the keyboard.

prompt: Which of these keep the form above the keyboard? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Modifier.imePadding() in Compose
choices.why: It pads by the ime inset.

choices.text: KeyboardAvoidingView in React Native
choices.why: It adjusts its height, position or bottom padding to the keyboard.

choices.text: SwiftUI's default layout
choices.why: It avoids the keyboard's safe area region unless told not to.

choices.text: .ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) in SwiftUI
choices.why: That lets the keyboard cover the view.

prompt: A long form cannot fit above the keyboard however the layout shrinks. Which of the two fixes fits?

choices.text: Shrinking the content area alone
choices.why: Shrinking leaves no room; the form needs to scroll.

choices.text: Hiding half of the fields while typing
choices.why: The lesson proposes no such thing.

choices.text: Scrolling, with the focused field brought into view
choices.why: Right. The content keeps its height and scrolls.

choices.text: Making the keyboard smaller in the app's code
choices.why: The app does not size the system's keyboard.

prompt: Why does KeyboardAvoidingView's own example choose 'padding' on iOS and 'height' on Android?

choices.text: Because Android has no software keyboard
choices.why: It has one; it is the ime inset.

choices.text: They respond differently to behavior
choices.why: Right, and the documentation recommends setting it on both.

choices.text: Because 'height' is faster to draw
choices.why: Speed is not the reason the documentation gives.

choices.text: Because iOS keyboards have a fixed height
choices.why: Keyboards change height; that is why they are reported as insets.

prompt: In the program's portrait example, how tall is the safe area?
In portrait with no keyboard, the button placed on the screen's edge lands at 780 to 828. Why is it reported as under the bottom inset?

choices.text: Because 828 is past the screen's height
choices.why: The screen is 844 tall; the button fits on it.

choices.text: Because the top inset is 48
choices.why: The top inset does not reach the bottom of the screen.

choices.text: Because the keyboard is up
choices.why: In that case the keyboard is 0.

choices.text: The bottom inset starts at 812
choices.why: Right. 844 minus 32 is 812, and the button reaches 828.

prompt: With a 300-tall keyboard, why does the program place the button at 480 to 528?

choices.text: It centres the button on the screen
choices.why: Nothing is centred; the button sits on an edge.

choices.text: It subtracts the keyboard from the top inset
choices.why: The top inset plays no part in this placement.

choices.text: 16 above the keyboard's top, at 844 minus 300
choices.why: Right. The higher of the two bottom edges is 544, so the button ends at 528.

choices.text: It scrolls the list by 300
choices.why: The program computes a position; it scrolls nothing.

prompt: What does the lesson say about the screen sizes, insets and keyboard height in insets.ts?

choices.text: They are examples, not device measurements
choices.why: Right. A real device reports its own.

choices.text: They are a particular iPhone's measured values
choices.why: No device was measured.

choices.text: They are what Android's documentation requires
choices.why: The documentation requires handling insets, not particular numbers.

choices.text: They were read from the computer's screen
choices.why: The program asks the computer nothing.

prompt: Order the steps that keep the add-session button visible when a field gets focus.
items: The keyboard appears and its height is reported as an inset
The form's bottom edge moves to the higher of the keyboard's top and the safe area's bottom
The layout is laid out again, or scrolled, in the space left
The keyboard closes and the form goes back to the safe area's bottom

prompt: The planner is turned to landscape and its list is drawn into the cutout at the left side, though it was fine in portrait. What did the code most likely do?

choices.text: Forgot the keyboard inset
choices.why: No keyboard is up in this case.

choices.text: Applied the insets twice
choices.why: That adds empty space; it does not draw into the cutout.

choices.text: Used dp instead of pixels
choices.why: dp is right; the problem is the insets.

choices.text: Read the insets once and kept them
choices.why: Right. In landscape the cutout moves to a side, and a stored top inset says nothing about it.

prompt: Which part of the planner's course screen may be drawn under the home indicator?

choices.text: The add-session button
choices.why: A control there competes with the system's gesture.

choices.text: The background
choices.why: Right. Background goes to the edges; content stays in the safe area.

choices.text: The last session's title
choices.why: Text there is covered by the handle.

choices.text: The keyboard
choices.why: The keyboard is the system's, not something the app draws.

prompt: On iOS, the part of a window not covered by hardware features or bars is called the safe ___.
